source_record.speaker: Quintus
source_record.source_account: Quintus discusses the attributed crow call on the left while defending the use of recorded signs.
source_record.qualifications: This initial chapterR7 clause continues section12, before section13. Favorable wording is not stated here; no flight polarity transferred. Latin label cornix checked independently; no modern scientific species inferred.

source_record.speaker: Quintus
source_record.source_account: Quintus discusses the attributed raven call on the right while defending the use of recorded signs.
source_record.qualifications: This initial chapterR7 clause continues section12, before section13. Favorable wording is not stated here; no flight polarity transferred. Latin label corvus checked independently; no modern scientific species inferred.

source_record.speaker: Quintus
source_record.source_account: Quintus cites an augur treating crow flight toward the left as favorable in a rhetorical defense of divination.
source_record.qualifications: Falconer renders flight to a side. Moving-to is the frozen digital comparison convention; merely located-on or departing-from is not silently equivalent. Historical favorable language is not a prediction for a user.

source_record.speaker: Quintus
source_record.source_account: Quintus cites an augur treating raven flight toward the right as favorable in a rhetorical defense of divination.
source_record.qualifications: Falconer renders flight to a side. Moving-to is the frozen digital comparison convention; merely located-on or departing-from is not silently equivalent. Historical favorable language is not a prediction for a user.

source_record.speaker: Falconer note226 as reproduced
source_record.source_account: The note gives a favorable right-side crow-call example, in conflict with the main-text left-side crow-call account.
source_record.qualifications: Editorial-note evidence only. A matching note is flagged conflicting_evidence, never promoted to a consensus main-text omen. No inferred observer heading.

observations.qualification: Voluntary contemporary/manual observations may be compared with a historical account. Neither a declared public setting nor a matched reference confers augural office, ritual validity or public decision authority.

context_references.speaker: Quintus
context_references.source_account: Alites give signs by flight and oscines by cries; Quintus connects their movements with divine will.
context_references.qualifications: Historical terminology, not automatic modern species classification or evidence of an actual divine intervention.

context_references.speaker: Falconer note133 as reproduced
context_references.source_account: The note supplies eagle,hawk,osprey as flight examples and raven,crow,owl as voice examples, with a Festus reference.
context_references.qualifications: Species examples belong to the note, not a separately verified original Cicero species list. Do not erase explicit corvid flight examples inI.39.85.

context_references.speaker: Cicero narrative introduction
context_references.source_account: The Roman account links augurs and auspices with royal foundation and the conduct of public business.
context_references.qualifications: Historical institutional description confers no public authority on a modern user observation.

context_references.speaker: Quintus
context_references.source_account: Quintus contrasts magistrates forced auspices with the reported loss or neglect of earlier augural practice.
context_references.qualifications: Ritual/institutional context, not a validated contemporary auspice procedure.

context_references.speaker: Marcus
context_references.source_account: Marcus questions contemporary use of bird divination and describes avoiding unwanted signs or their observation.
context_references.qualifications: Criticism and reported practice remain attributed; the engine does not authenticate or perform public auspices.

context_references.speaker: Marcus
context_references.source_account: Marcus contrasts national side conventions and favorable sinistra language, including signs physically on the right, while challenging consistency.
context_references.qualifications: Sinistra as a favorable expression is not a universal physical-left rule. No unified Roman/Greek direction or compass map.

context_references.speaker: Falconer note226 as reproduced
context_references.source_account: The note describes Roman observers facing south and Greek observers facing north; its crow-right example conflicts with the main-text crow-left account.
context_references.qualifications: This note is retained as documentary evidence, not an executable observer-orientation rule or permission to fill missing headings.

context_references.speaker: Marcus
context_references.source_account: Marcus challenges a victory interpretation of crowing cocks and considers ordinary or chance causes, including an attributed Democritus digestion explanation.
context_references.qualifications: Neither victory prophecy nor the ancient physiological account is independently established modern biology.

context_references.speaker: Quintus
context_references.source_account: Quintus introduces natural/weather-sign analogies outside divination, including quoted bird behaviors.
context_references.qualifications: No operational forecast, bird-species diagnosis or copied Aeromancy rule. Historical/weather analogy is separate from source augural matching.

translation_notes.latin_clause: a dextra corvus, a sinistra cornix faciat ratum
translation_notes.qualification: The inspected Latin clause names sides/birds and ratum, without an explicit flight verb. Falconer English supplies flies/to. This profile deliberately matches the1923 English flight-to wording; it does not claim an independently established original-Latin velocity or universal ancient side convention.
translation_notes.call_qualification: Latin call verb canere explicitly present; section12 continues into chapterVII before13.
translation_notes.source_access: Primary Latin web rendering inspected; no successful fresh raw-byte snapshot/printed edition. No silent correction of Latin/English differences.

conventions.call_relation: located_on_side for the translated call-on-side account
conventions.flight_relation: moving_to_side for Falconer flight-to-side; located-on and moving-from are distinct and not coerced
conventions.frame: observer_relative is an explicitly declared qualitative digital comparison frame, not an ancient orientation theorem; unknown frame insufficient, cardinal frame unsupported
conventions.polarity: Only explicit main-text favorable flight accounts are listed as main-text favorable matches; calls retain not_stated. Note favorable text remains conflicting editorial evidence.
conventions.source_conflict: Crow-call comparison on either supported side exposes note226/main-text disagreement without changing the main-text condition. Applicable source record and conflicting overall evidence can coexist.
conventions.observation_conflict: Structured side reports disagreeing with one another or the declared side block a positive match. Raw prose is not interpreted for contradictions.
conventions.unknowns: Known mismatches exclude exact conditions; unknown/uncertain required fields remain insufficient. Unknown species and cardinal conversion unsupported, never unfavorable.

evaluation_policy: Unrecognized bird unsupported. Known mismatches in bird/phenomenon/side/relation exclude a condition. Structured side conflict blocks positive matching; cardinal frame unsupported; unknown/uncertain required fields insufficient. Note226 full match remains conflicting. Overall crow-call main match also exposes source disagreement without altering its main-text match.
